_comment: Independent fitness table for build_dispatch_plan()'s _select_workflow(),
authored per Proposal 03 of the orchestration review.
PURPOSE: selection_golden_corpus.json pins build_dispatch_plan()'s current
output as its own regression baseline -- it is derived FROM the code and
therefore cannot catch the code mislabeling something, because a bug in
_select_workflow() and a fixture copied from that same buggy output will
always agree. This file is deliberately NOT derived from _select_workflow()
or from the golden corpus. Every 'expected_workflow' value below was
reasoned independently from roster/workflows/*.md (the human-authored
description of what each workflow shape means) and from routing.yaml's
route/risk semantics, then checked against selection.schema.json's closed
'workflow' enum. Where an entry's task/changed_files were reused from
selection_golden_corpus.json or test_selector.py (to guarantee a known
route/risk match without re-deriving routing.yaml's matching rules), the
'reasoning' field says so explicitly -- reuse of INPUT text is fine;
copying the EXPECTED OUTPUT would defeat the point of this file.
test_workflow_fitness_table.py runs build_dispatch_plan() against every
case here and asserts actual workflow == expected_workflow. Two cases are
deliberately expected to disagree with current code (see their 'reasoning'
and 'known_mismatch' fields) -- that disagreement is the entire point of
this file: it is proof the table is independent, not a copy of the bug.
Coverage: at least one case per selection.schema.json workflow enum value
(new-service, product-intake, runtime-assurance, debugging,
infrastructure-change, pipeline-change, knowledge-ingestion,
support-escalation, production-release, rollback, unclassified,
needs-triage).
Scope boundary: this file does not add a new workflow enum value, does
not modify _select_workflow(), and does not add a roster/workflows/*.md
doc. If a case below implies the closed enum is genuinely missing a
shape, that is Proposal 08's territory, not this file's -- see the PR
description for which cases (if any) that applies to.

cases.task: Implement a backend API for user upload
cases.reasoning: new-service.md: 'covers work that proceeds beyond intake into design and delivery.' A backend route match (one of the build-shaped routes: frontend/backend/infrastructure/pipeline) implementing a new API endpoint is squarely design-and-delivery work, not a narrower recognized shape (not infra/pipeline-only, not a defect fix, not intake-only). Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's BACKEND-1 to guarantee the route match; the expected workflow value was derived independently from new-service.md, not copied from BACKEND-1's (unasserted) workflow.

cases.description: architecture-change risk with no build-shaped route -> new-service
cases.task: Design the architecture and system design proposal
cases.reasoning: new-service.md step 3 names the architecture phase (Cloud Architect, G3) as an explicit stage of this same lifecycle shape, so a task that trips routing.yaml's 'architecture-change' risk rule (System Architect boundary/ADR work) belongs to new-service even when no frontend/backend/infrastructure/pipeline route also matched. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's ARCHITECTURE-DESIGN-1.

cases.task: Capture the product intent for the new mission objective
cases.reasoning: product-intake.md: 'Use this workflow when work has not yet entered architecture or implementation.' Drafting the versioned intent record is literally step 2 of product-intake.md, before any G2/architecture handoff. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's PRODUCT-INTENT-1.

cases.task: Perform requirements decomposition and requirements traceability
cases.reasoning: product-intake.md step 4: Requirements Agent decomposes approved intent into requirement IDs/acceptance criteria/traceability -- the requirements-baseline route's own G1/G2 quality_gates in routing.yaml match product-intake.md's G1/G2 handoff, still strictly before new-service.md's G3 architecture stage. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's REQUIREMENTS-BASELINE-1.

cases.task: Observe production runtime conformance for deployed behavior
cases.reasoning: runtime-assurance.md's own flowchart (Observability SRE observes -> Security/Compliance review -> G10 Service Owner decides) is precisely this task's shape. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's RUNTIME-ASSURANCE-1.

cases.description: backend+testing+debugging routes, explicit defect investigation -> debugging
cases.task: Debug a panic and identify the root cause from the stack trace
cases.reasoning: debugging.md step 2: 'Reproduce the issue or prove it is unreproducible, isolate the smallest likely cause.' This task is a textbook reproduce/root-cause/fix case -- an actual defect, not routine maintenance (contrast with WF-AGENT-SUITE-GOVERNANCE-MISLABEL-1 below). Task/file reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's DEBUGGING-1.

cases.task: Update Terraform for a Proxmox worker VM
cases.reasoning: infrastructure-change.md's Classify -> Provision+Plan -> Infrastructure Reviewer -> gated approval -> Apply shape is exactly an IaC-only change with no frontend/backend/pipeline overlap. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's INFRA-1.
cases.known_gate: infrastructure-change.md cross-checks G3/G4/G5/G6/G7/G8 against routing.yaml's infrastructure route -- consistent with no risk rule firing here.

cases.task: Change the GitLab pipeline runner configuration
cases.reasoning: pipeline-change.md's Document -> Test -> Pipeline Security Reviewer -> gated approval -> Enable shape covers exactly a CI/CD runner-configuration change. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's PIPELINE-1.

cases.task: Tune the knowledge store retrieval and embedding vector search
cases.reasoning: knowledge-ingestion.md's Record -> Security/Compliance review -> Normalize -> Redact -> Ingest -> Evaluate -> Evidence shape is the recognized shape for knowledge-store-only work; nothing else (no frontend/backend/infra/pipeline/debugging) also matched. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's KNOWLEDGE-STORE-1.

cases.task: Provide user report triage and a workaround for a customer issue
cases.reasoning: support-escalation.md's Triage -> Investigate -> Escalate -> Closure shape is exactly a customer-ticket triage/workaround task. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's SUPPORT-1.

cases.description: incident-response route, task mentions 'rollback' but the action described is coordination/escalation, not execution -> support-escalation, NOT rollback
cases.task: Coordinate rollback during a sev1 major incident postmortem
cases.reasoning: Deliberately placed next to WF-ROLLBACK-GAP-1 below to show the two are genuinely different shapes, not the same shape mislabeled two different ways. This task's verb is 'coordinate' during a sev1/postmortem/war-room incident -- that is support-escalation.md's Triage/Investigate/Escalate/'Human escalation' shape (an accountable human decides on the production action while the incident is being managed). rollback.md instead describes the release engineer's concrete execution playbook ('Release engineer selects the pre-approved rollback... obtain emergency authorization... deploy known-good artifact') once a decision has already been made. Incident coordination is not artifact-rollback execution, so support-escalation is the correct label for this specific task text even though it contains the word 'rollback'. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's INCIDENT-RESPONSE-1.

production-release.md's G8 precondition-check -> G9 deploy-immutable-artifact -> verify -> G10 shape matches routing.yaml's 'production' risk rule (deploy/release/production keyword groups) exactly. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's PRODUCTION-RISK-1.

cases.description: an explicit rollback-execution task; fixed in #157 by a rollback route plus a branch ahead of the production risk check
cases.task: Roll back the production release to the last known-good artifact after failed verification
cases.reasoning: rollback.md's Trigger -> Preserve Evidence -> Release Engineer selects known-good procedure -> emergency human authorization -> Deploy known-good artifact -> Verify shape is exactly this task. Before #157 'rollback' was an enumerated, documented workflow no plan could be assigned: the production risk check ran first and swallowed it. The branch now runs ahead of that check, and excludes incident-coordination framing so a task merely mentioning rollback stays support-escalation.

cases.description: governance-planning route only, no recognized shape -> unclassified
cases.task: Assess governance impact and data jurisdiction
cases.reasoning: unclassified.md: emitted when 'the selector matched at least one route or risk rule... but the matched combination does not fit any of this repository's recognized workflow shapes.' governance-planning is a narrow advisory/review route with its own AGENT.md but no dedicated roster/workflows/*.md shape (it contributes to new-service.md step 2 as one participant among several, but is never itself a whole recognized shape). Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's GOVERNANCE-PLANNING-1.

AGENTS.md/RUNBOOK.md: 'If no rule matches a task, the selector returns needs-triage rather than guessing.' Trivial by construction: no selected agents means _select_workflow()'s first check (`if not has_agents: return "needs-triage"`) is the only defensible answer. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's NEEDS-TRIAGE-1.

cases.description: routine roster/catalog maintenance with no defect present -- the review's named case, fixed by PR #154's agent-suite-maintenance workflow
cases.task: add a new specialist role to the roster
cases.reasoning: agent-suite-maintenance.md covers maintenance of this repository's own role catalog, routing rules, and orchestration tooling -- work where the roster machinery is the subject, not the tool. Adding a role is exactly that. Before #154 this returned 'debugging', because _select_workflow() mapped every agent-suite-governance match there unconditionally; that branch now distinguishes a keyword-driven debugging hit from a path-only roster edit, so a routine catalog change no longer reads as defect investigation.

cases.task: Add a React upload form backed by a PostgreSQL API
cases.reasoning: Same reasoning as WF-NEW-SERVICE-1, extended to confirm a multi-route build case (frontend+backend) still resolves to the single new-service shape rather than being treated as ambiguous. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's CROSS-STACK-1.
